prior_rounds.blocking_finding: project_tree_ensure_dir force-unmounted and took over a link path already bound (bind_rc==2) to something other than the computed ext4_dir, with no identity check -- contradicting the task's own guard and LINUX_SHELL_RULES.md #3.

project_tree_bind_state (:194-201 at the time) returned 0 ('confirmed bound') for any mountpoint at the link path whenever the ext4 target directory had never been created yet, instead of failing closed -- a fresh project's very first ensure/status call could silently misreport a foreign mount as the script's own correct bind.

notes: Round 3 closes the BIND-STATE-IDENTITY-GAP finding from round 2. project_tree_bind_state now returns 2 (the same fail-closed path bind_rc==2 already used for a confirmed-different bind) whenever the link path is a mountpoint but ext4_dir does not exist yet, instead of returning 0 on the strength of 'nothing proved it isn't ours'. Independently re-verified live in a private mount namespace on this session's own Linux host (unprivileged bind mounts via `unshare --mount --map-root-user`, not WSL -- this reviewer's environment is native Debian, not Windows+WSL, so this is the equivalent isolated-scratch substitute for the WSL Debian runs earlier rounds used): (1) reproduced the exact round-2 repro (fresh project, ext4_dir absent, a foreign bind already on node_modules) -- project_tree_bind_state now returns 2, status reports 'bound, but NOT confirmed ... does not exist yet', ensure skips with a warning and creates nothing, the foreign mount and its content are left untouched; (2) a happy-path regression pass (fresh project, no foreign mount) confirms ensure still creates the ext4 dir and binds correctly, a second ensure reports 'already bound' with no unmount/remount, and release correctly unmounts and resurfaces the original content. No other function changed. All three findings across all three rounds are now closed with no open blocker.

The function's own comment block (:192-200) was rewritten to state the fail-closed rule explicitly ('this must fail closed ... instead of failing open the way returning 0 here unconditionally once did'), matching the round-2 finding's own reasoning almost verbatim. BIND-STATE-IDENTITY-GAP-INDEPENDENTLY-VE.detail: Live test in a private mount namespace (`unshare --mount --map-root-user --propagation private`, scratch dirs under /tmp, cleaned up after): built the exact round-2 repro -- a fresh scratch repo (node_modules never ensured before, so its ext4_dir does not exist on disk) with a genuine `mount --bind` from an unrelated 'foreign_source' directory placed directly onto node_modules. Direct call: `project_tree_bind_state "$link_path" "$ext4_dir"` now returns 2 (previously 0). `project_tree_main status` reports 'bound, but NOT confirmed as <ext4_dir> (different source, or <ext4_dir> does not exist yet)', not the false-positive 'bound -> <ext4_dir>' round 2 reproduced. `project_tree_main ensure` prints the skip+warning ('already a mountpoint bound to something other than <ext4_dir> -- leaving it alone') and takes no action: <ext4_dir> was confirmed still absent afterward, the mount was confirmed still the foreign source (mountpoint -q true, foreign.txt still readable through it, dev:ino unchanged), and a second status call after ensure was unchanged. Final `umount`/`rm -rf` cleanup left nothing behind.

HAPPY-PATH-REGRESSION.detail: Separate scratch run, no foreign mount, same private-mount-namespace technique: first `ensure` on a fresh project correctly creates <ext4_dir> and binds ('[project-tree] bound ... -> ...'); `status` afterward reports 'bound -> <ext4_dir>'; a second `ensure` reports 'already bound' with no unmount/remount (idempotency intact, the fix did not make the identity check over-eager); `ls` on the bound path shows the ext4 content, not the original marker.txt (bind is active); `release` unmounts and the original marker.txt resurfaces. The fail-closed fix has no observable effect on the already-correct legitimate path -- it only changes the previously-unverifiable 'ext4_dir absent' branch.

ROUND1-AND-ROUND2-STILL-INTACT.detail: project_tree_ensure_dir's bind_rc==2 handling (round 1's fix: skip+warn, never force-unmount/take over) is unchanged and still reachable via project_tree_bind_state's new rc==2 return for the 'ext4_dir absent' case too -- the same code path now correctly covers both sub-cases of rc==2 (confirmed-different, and cannot-verify). No regression to the round-1 fix; re-confirmed by the happy-path and foreign-mount live tests above, both of which exercise project_tree_ensure_dir directly.

NTFS-SAFETY.detail: The fail-closed change only ever causes the function to return early with no action (mkdir/mount) taken -- it cannot itself cause a write, delete, or takeover. Confirmed live: the foreign-mount scenario resulted in zero mkdir/mount/umount calls from ensure.
